narrative:
The model determined that you have a 47% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability is high enough to cross the bank's threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the purpose of the loan, the amount you requested, and the status of your checking account. The fact that you are borrowing to buy a new car pushed the prediction toward bad credit risk; new-car loans are associated with higher risk compared with other uses such as home-related purchases that dominate the approved group. Your requested loan of 6,260 DM also worked against you. This is more than twice the average amount approved applicants typically request, and larger loans increase the model's concern about repayment. Finally, having a checking-account balance between 0 and 200 DM added further risk in the model's view. While many approved applicants have no checking account at all, those who do maintain only small balances like yours tend to be seen as less stable.

Taken together, these three elements outweighed several positive signals such as your solid credit history of bills paid on time and your steady employment of four to seven years.

To improve your chances on a future application, consider applying for a smaller loan, perhaps for a different purpose, and wait until your checking-account balance is higher. Strengthening these areas will help move future predictions in a more favorable direction. (218 words)
